**Quarto OS** renders macOS-style windows — title bar with traffic lights, rounded
corners, soft shadows — around anything you write in Markdown: images, videos, code,
callouts. And it ships *apps*: a **terminal**, a **VS Code**-like editor and a
**Finder**-like file explorer, all connected to **one real Linux VM running in the
reader's browser**. No server, no accounts, nothing to install for your students.

The windows above are plain Markdown and you can drag them around by their title bars.

::: {.feature-grid}

::: {.feature}
### Windows for any content
Wrap images, video, code blocks or callouts in a window. Inline, side by side, or
floating and draggable.
:::

::: {.feature}
### A real terminal
`bash` in a Debian VM powered by [CheerpX](https://cheerpx.io). `git`, `python3`,
`vim` and friends just work — offline, in the browser.
:::

::: {.feature}
### VS Code & Explorer
A Monaco-based editor and a file explorer that show the *same* files your terminal
just changed — including hidden ones like `.git`.
:::

::: {.feature}
### Desktops, docks & slides
A fake desktop with menubar and dock, launch buttons, clickable run snippets and
full reveal.js support.
:::

:::

## Try it {#try-it}

This is a small desktop. Drag the windows, then click an icon in the dock to open a
terminal, the editor or the file explorer. The first VM app you open boots a Debian VM
in your browser (it downloads a few megabytes on the first visit), every further app
attaches to the same machine.

::: {.os-desktop #home-desk height="440px" title="Quarto OS"}

::: {.os-window title="Welcome.md" x=28 y=24 width=360 height=270}
**Welcome!** This desktop is written in Markdown. Try to:

- **drag** a window by its title bar,
- click the **dock** to open a terminal, VS Code or the explorer,
- open **several** terminals — they all share one VM.

## Install {#install}

Quarto OS is a Quarto filter extension. In your project directory run:

```bash
quarto add jansim/quarto-os
```

This installs the extension into `_extensions/quarto-os/` (commit that folder with
your project). Then enable the filter, either for a single document or for a whole
project in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
filters:
  - quarto-os
```

It works with `format: html` (documents and websites) and `format: revealjs`.

## Quick start {#quick-start}

````markdown
---
title: "My first lesson"
filters:
  - quarto-os
---

::: {.os-window title="hello.py"}
```python
print("Hello from a window!")
```
:::

::: {#shell .os-window app="terminal" height="300px"}
:::

Click to run it: `python3 -c 'print("Hello from Linux!")'`{.os-run target="shell"}
````

Render or preview as usual (`quarto preview my-lesson.qmd`). The first window is pure
HTML/CSS. The second one is a real terminal: the page lazily loads the VM, boots
Debian and starts `bash`. Clicking the snippet types the command into the terminal and
presses <kbd>Enter</kbd>.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Previewing locally
The VM needs a *cross-origin isolated* page. `quarto preview` doesn't send the required
headers, so Quarto OS registers a small service worker that adds them and reloads the
page once. Everything else is automatic — see [Limitations](#limitations).
:::

## Reference {#reference}

### Windows

A window is a fenced div with the class `.os-window`. Everything inside it is regular
Markdown and becomes the window's content:

````markdown
::: {.os-window title="cat.jpg" width="420px" height="300px"}
![](cat.jpg)
:::

::: {.os-window title="hello.py"}
```python
print("hi")
```
:::
````

With an `app` attribute the window becomes an application instead (the div is left
empty). Every app can also be written as an `os` shortcode, which is handy inline or in
slides:

````markdown
::: {#t1 .os-window app="terminal" height="320px" cwd="~/repo" run="git status"}
:::

{{{< os terminal title="bash" height="300px" >}}}
{{{< os vscode folder="~/repo" open="README.md" >}}}
{{{< os explorer path="~" >}}}
{{{< os browser url="https://quarto.org" >}}}
````

#### Window attributes

All attributes are optional.

| Attribute | Meaning |
|----------|------------------------------------------|
| `app` | `content` (default; wraps the div's Markdown), `terminal`, `vscode`, `explorer` or `browser` |
| `title` | Title bar text (default: the app's name) |
| `width`, `height` | Any CSS length (`420px`, `60%`, `50vh`); bare numbers mean pixels |
| `x`, `y` | Position in pixels when the window floats (inside a desktop, a slide, or with `float=true`) |
| `float` | `true` → absolutely positioned and draggable over its container instead of in the text flow |
| `#id` | An id, e.g. `{#t1 .os-window …}`; used as `target` by run snippets and launchers |
| `theme` | `light` or `dark` window chrome (default from the document option `quarto-os: theme`) |
| `state` | `normal`, `minimized` or `maximized` (inside a desktop) |

#### App-specific attributes

| App | Attribute | Meaning |
|----------|----------|------------------------------------|
| `terminal` | `cwd` | Working directory the shell starts in |
| | `run` | Command typed after the shell has started; `;`-separated commands are fine |
| `vscode` | `folder` | Workspace root shown in the editor's file tree |
| | `open` | Comma-separated files (relative to `folder`) opened as tabs |
| `explorer` | `path` | Start directory |
| | `hidden` | Show dotfiles such as `.git` (default `true`) |
| `browser` | `url` | Page shown in the window (see [Limitations](#limitations) for third-party sites) |

Paths may start with `~`, which means the VM user's home directory `/home/user`.

::: {.callout-note}
## Floating windows
`x` and `y` are relative to the closest positioned container. Inside a desktop or a
reveal.js slide that's the desktop/slide; for `float=true` windows in a normal page,
wrap them in a div with `position: relative` and a height (the examples use a small
`.stage` class for this).
:::

### Desktop

A `.os-desktop` div renders a fake desktop with wallpaper, menubar and dock. Windows
nested inside it become floating windows on the desktop:

````markdown
::: {#desk .os-desktop height="520px" dock="terminal,vscode,explorer"}

::: {.os-window app="terminal" x=40 y=40 width=520 height=300}
:::

:::
````

| Attribute | Meaning |
|----------|------------------------------------------|
| `#id` | Id used as `target` by launchers |
| `height` | Desktop height (default `480px`) |
| `dock` | Comma-separated apps shown in the dock (default `terminal,vscode,explorer`); each click opens a new instance |
| `menubar` | `true`/`false` — show the menubar (default `true`) |
| `title` | App name shown in the menubar |
| `wallpaper` | Background image URL |

### Launchers

A span with the class `.os-launch` becomes a button. Each click opens a **new** window;
any window attribute can be given:

```markdown
[New terminal]{.os-launch app="terminal" target="desk" cwd="~/repo"}
[Edit the README]{.os-launch app="vscode" folder="~/repo" open="README.md"}
```

Where does the window go? With `target`, into that desktop. Without it: inside a
reveal.js slide → floating on that slide; otherwise into the page's desktop if there is
exactly one; otherwise floating over the page.

### Run snippets

Add `.os-run` to inline code or a code block to make it clickable. A click sends the
text plus <kbd>Enter</kbd> to a terminal:

````markdown
`git status`{.os-run target="t1"}

```{.bash .os-run target="t1"}
git add README.md
git commit -m "First commit"
```
````

The terminal is chosen like this: the window with id `target`; otherwise the most
recently focused terminal; otherwise a new floating terminal is opened.

### Document options

Options go under `quarto-os:` in the document front matter or in `_quarto.yml`. All
are optional:

```yaml
quarto-os:
  theme: light            # default window chrome: light | dark
  coi: true               # register coi-serviceworker.js on pages that use the VM
  vm:
    disk: wss://disks.webvm.io/debian_buster_large_permis_fixed_01-06-2026.ext2
    disk-type: cloud      # cloud | github | bytes
    persist: false        # keep disk changes across reloads (IndexedDB)
    cache-id: quarto-os   # IndexedDB name for the disk overlay
    autoboot: false       # boot on page load instead of on the first VM window
    setup: |              # bash script, run once per fresh VM as `user`
      mkdir -p ~/repo
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|----------|----------|------------------------------------|
| `theme` | `light` | Default window chrome theme |
| `coi` | `true` | Make VM pages cross-origin isolated with a service worker. Set to `false` if your server already sends `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` and `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` |
| `vm.disk` | WebVM's Debian image | Disk image URL |
| `vm.disk-type` | `cloud` | `cloud` (streamed over WebSocket), `github` (chunked image hosted with your site) or `bytes` (plain HTTP with range requests) |
| `vm.persist` | `false` | Keep changes to the disk in IndexedDB so they survive reloads |
| `vm.cache-id` | `quarto-os` | Name of the IndexedDB overlay — use different ids for unrelated lessons |
| `vm.autoboot` | `false` | Boot the VM as soon as the page loads |
| `vm.setup` | — | Shell script run once in a fresh VM before any app attaches. Perfect for `git config`, sample files and folders |

### JavaScript API

Everything is also scriptable from your own `<script>` tags through `window.QuartoOS`:

```js
// open a new terminal floating over the page and run a command in it
const win = await QuartoOS.open("terminal", { cwd: "~", run: "ls -la" });

// send a command to the terminal with id "t1"
QuartoOS.run("git log --oneline", "t1");

// talk to the VM directly
const vm = await QuartoOS.vm();
await vm.writeFile("~/notes.txt", "Hello!\n");
const { output } = await vm.exec("wc -c notes.txt", { cwd: "~" });
```

## How the VM works {#how-it-works}

**CheerpX in the browser.** The apps are backed by
[CheerpX](https://cheerpx.io), the x86-to-WebAssembly virtualization engine by Leaning
Technologies that also powers [WebVM](https://webvm.io). It runs an unmodified 32-bit
**Debian** (i386) — with `bash`, `git`, `python3`, `nano`, `vim` and the usual
command-line tools — entirely in the reader's browser. Nothing runs on a server and
nothing a student types leaves their machine.

**One VM per page.** All terminals, editors and explorers on a page talk to the *same*
machine. A file created in one terminal immediately shows up in the explorer and in
VS Code; a commit made in the terminal shows up in the editor's source control. A tiny
agent inside the VM (`qos-agent`, a 48 KB static C binary) serves the file operations
and starts the shells; each terminal runs on its own CheerpX virtual console, so
keystrokes go straight to `bash` without any extra hop.

**Streaming disk.** The disk image is not downloaded up front: CheerpX fetches only the
blocks that are actually read and caches them in the browser, so the first boot takes
a few seconds longer and later visits are fast. Changes are kept in memory and vanish
on reload, unless `vm.persist: true` stores them in IndexedDB.

**Lazy loading.** Every page only loads the small core (`quarto-os.js` +
`quarto-os.css`, about 60 KB before compression). The heavy parts — xterm.js for terminals, Monaco
(the editor of VS Code) for the editor, CheerpX and the VM layer — are loaded the
first time a window needs them, e.g. when a terminal scrolls into view or someone
clicks a dock icon. Pages with only content windows never download any of it.

**Cross-origin isolation.** CheerpX needs `SharedArrayBuffer`, which browsers only
enable on *cross-origin isolated* pages. Static hosts such as GitHub Pages can't set
the required headers, so pages that use the VM register
[coi-serviceworker](https://github.com/gzuidhof/coi-serviceworker), which adds them and
reloads the page once on the first visit.

## Teaching tips {#teaching-tips}

- **Prepare the machine with `vm.setup`.** Configure `git` identities (the default is
  `Student <student@example.com>`, so commits work out of the box), create folders
  and starter files so every student starts from exactly the same state. A reload gives
  everyone a fresh, clean machine (unless you enable `persist`).
- **Make the invisible visible.** Put a terminal next to an Explorer with hidden files
  shown: students *see* `.git` appear after `git init` and files vanish when they switch
  branches. The [git lesson](examples/git-lesson.qmd) is built around this.
- **Click first, type later.** `.os-run` snippets let beginners follow along without
  typos. Encourage them to type the next commands themselves — it's a real shell.
- **Name your terminals.** With several terminals on a page, give each an `#id` and
  use `target` so snippets end up in the right one.
- **Warm up before class.** Open the page once before the lecture so the VM engine and
  disk blocks are cached; for talks consider `autoboot: true` on the slide deck.
- **Have a fallback.** Keep a screenshot or recording handy for classroom machines with
  old or locked-down browsers.

## Limitations {#limitations}

- **One reload on first visit.** Pages that use the VM are made cross-origin isolated by
  a service worker, which needs one automatic reload the first time a page is opened.
  Serving your site with the COOP/COEP headers yourself avoids it (`coi: false`).
- **No third-party iframes on VM pages.** Under COEP, embeds like YouTube videos, maps
  or other sites' pages (including the `browser` app pointing at them) are blocked on
  pages that use the VM. Self-host such media or put it on a page without VM apps.
  Pages with only content windows are not affected.
- **At most six terminals at once.** CheerpX provides six virtual consoles, so a page
  can have up to six terminals (including VS Code's integrated terminal) open at the
  same time; a seventh shows a message asking to close one. Terminals in windows that
  never scrolled into view don't count.
- **No network inside the VM.** `apt install`, `pip install`, `curl` or `git clone`
  from the internet don't work. Create what you need in `vm.setup`, or use a custom
  disk image that already contains it.
- **First boot downloads.** The VM engine and the disk blocks it touches are downloaded
  on first use (several megabytes); afterwards they come from the browser cache.
- **An older Debian.** The default image is Debian buster (i386): e.g. git 2.20, which
  predates `git switch`/`git restore` — use `git checkout`.
- **Browsers.** Recent Chromium-based browsers (Chrome, Edge, Brave…) and Firefox are
  recommended. Other browsers and phones may work but are slower and use a lot of
  memory.

## Licensing {#licensing}

Quarto OS bundles or loads several third-party components:

- **CheerpX** is proprietary software by [Leaning Technologies](https://leaningtech.com).
  It is free for personal use and for open-source projects; **commercial or
  organizational use requires a license** from Leaning Technologies — see
  [cheerpx.io](https://cheerpx.io). Quarto OS loads it at runtime from Leaning

- The default disk image is a Debian system hosted by the WebVM project; the software

- [xterm.js](https://xtermjs.org), [Monaco Editor](https://microsoft.github.io/monaco-editor/)
